Every topic page would render broken images, and check:figures passes silently. specs/content/gqur-301/figures/unit-15.md fig-U15-3 prompt and docs/semester-2/gqur-301/unit-15/topic-02.mdx fig-U15-3 alt: the figure marks z = 1.82 inside a two-tailed "do not reject" region, but it opens Topic 15.2, whose only worked example computes z = 1.84 for a right-tailed test and rejects H0 (p = 0.0329). A learner meets a figure that contradicts both the statistic and the decision. Repair: draw the right-tailed test (critical z = 1.645, z = 1.84 in the shaded rejection region) or explicitly label it a two-tailed variant of the same data with z = 1.84 and p = 0.065; update alt text and prompt together.

specs/content/gqur-301/figures/unit-15.md fig-U15-2 prompt and docs/semester-2/gqur-301/unit-15/topic-01.mdx fig-U15-2 alt: says the observed mean 75 "falls in the right tail" beside shaded two-tailed rejection regions, implying rejection; the two-tailed critical mean is 72 + 1.96 x 1.69 = 75.31, so 75 lies just inside the non-rejection region (consistent with the topic's decision, p = 0.075). The prompt also asks for "the area beyond it ... labelled p/2 on each side", which conflates the p-value area with the 0.025 rejection areas. Repair: mark the critical values (about 68.7 and 75.3), place 75 just inside them, label the area beyond 75 (and its mirror below 69) as p/2 = 0.038, and rewrite the alt text to say 75 does not reach the rejection region.

docs/semester-2/gqur-301/unit-15/unit-assessment.mdx, ERQ 2 rubric key: wrong and self-contradictory. For z = 2.10 the two-tailed p is 0.0357 (0.036) and the one-tailed p is 0.0179. Teacher A's p is therefore the correct two-tailed value; A's only error is the causal claim "the new method works". The key instead says A "treats the one-tailed p-value as if the test is two-tailed" and in the next sentence that a two-tailed test with z = 2.10 gives 0.036. For Teacher B the key says the two-tailed p "would become 0.072" and be non-significant; in fact B mislabels 0.036 as one-tailed (it is 0.018), and the required two-tailed p = 0.036 < 0.05 is significant, so B's conclusion is wrong. The Error-in-A rubric row ("tail mismatch") would reward an incorrect answer. Repair: rewrite the key and rubric rows on these values.

docs/semester-2/gqur-301/unit-15/unit-assessment.mdx, RRQ 10 model answer: "1 - (0.95 x 0.05) ~ 0.0975" evaluates to 0.9525; the correct expression is 1 - 0.95^2 = 1 - 0.9025 = 0.0975 (independent tests). A learner who copies the printed working gets a probability above 0.95. Repair: write 1 - 0.95 x 0.95 = 0.0975.

Citations in docs/semester-2/gqur-301/unit-15/topic-01.mdx, topic-02.mdx, topic-03.mdx (Further reading and in-text locators): 6 of 9 deep links are broken or point to unrelated pages (see crew-20261023/source-inspection.md). Substance is supported by OpenStax 9.1/9.3 and Lane 11 Significance Testing. Repair: replace each URL and locator with the real page (e.g. onlinestatbook.com/2/logic_of_hypothesis_testing/significance.html, onlinestatbook.com/2/tests_of_means/single_mean.html, OpenStax 9.3), correct sources/unit-15.md, and bind the passages under sources/texts/.
